distinguishing_feature: [LLM DRAFT] Typically presents with disseminated central nervous system lesions in space and time rather than an isolated spinal cord syndrome.
[LLM DRAFT] Presents with dermatomal pain and radicular symptoms rather than a distinct spinal cord sensory level and bilateral motor deficits.
[LLM DRAFT] Involves isolated unilateral visual loss and afferent pupillary defect rather than acute transverse myelopathy symptoms.
[LLM DRAFT] Permanent rather than transient monocular or binocular vision loss often associated with cherry-red spot on fundoscopic examination
[LLM DRAFT] Subacute painful loss of vision with relative afferent pupillary defect rather than painless transient obscurations
[LLM DRAFT] Visual symptoms typically present as a spreading fortification spectrum and are accompanied by headache and positive migrainous features
[LLM DRAFT] Presence of sensory deficits and disseminated central nervous system lesions separated in space and time
[LLM DRAFT] Pain and sensory symptoms typically restricted to a specific dermatomal distribution without widespread lower motor neuron signs
[LLM DRAFT] Characterized by profound fatigue, post-exertional malaise, and cognitive difficulties without progressive motor neuron degeneration
